content: A wart is a small, rough growth on the skin, often found on the hands and feet. It may resemble a cauliflower or a solid blister. Warts are caused by an infection with the human papillomavirus (HPV) and are contagious. They can spread through direct skin contact with an infected person or by sharing objects like towels. While warts often resolve on their own within a few months, they can persist for years and may recur. Certain types of HPV are also associated with the development of cervical cancer. Warts typically present as raised, round, or oval growths on the skin with a rough texture. They may appear lighter, darker, or occasionally black compared to the surrounding skin. Most adults can easily identify a wart based on its appearance. However, warts with smooth surfaces or flat warts, particularly in children, may be harder to recognize. Some warts resolve spontaneously without medical intervention, but this process can take years. Even after disappearing, warts may recur. Warts can spread from one area of the body to another. If a wart is unsightly or causes discomfort, treatment options are available. Warts located around or beneath the nails are particularly challenging to treat compared to those in other areas. To prevent warts, it is important to avoid direct skin contact with someone who has a wart. This can help reduce the risk of infection.
